sections.label: Bill and Apostille Convention
sections.summary: The Bill gives effect to Apostille Convention obligations domestically so Singapore can become a Contracting Party.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill gives effect to the obligations under the Apostille Convention domestically, so that Singapore can become a Contracting Party.

sections.label: Contracting Party obligations
sections.summary: When Singapore becomes a Contracting Party in 2021, other Contracting Parties must waive legalisation and accept Singapore's apostilles.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: When Singapore becomes a Contracting Party to the Apostille Convention in 2021, other Contracting Parties will be obliged to waive the legalisation requirement for public documents issued by Singapore authorities and must accept the apostilles issued by Singapore's designated Competent Authority.

sections.label: SAL as Competent Authority
sections.summary: The Singapore Academy of Law will be designated Competent Authority and authorised to issue apostille certificates on Singapore public documents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In this case, the Singapore Academy of Law or SAL will be designated as Singapore's Competent Authority under the Convention and will be authorised to issue apostille certificates on Singapore public documents as defined in clause 14 of the Bill.

sections.label: SAL takes over legalisation
sections.summary: SAL is expected to take over the legalisation function from MFA by January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SAL is expected to take over the legalisation function from MFA by January 2021.

sections.label: Presumption for apostilled documents
sections.summary: Clause 11 presumes a foreign public document's origin sufficiently proven unless the contrary is established, covering signature, capacity and seal.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 11 of the Bill provides that the origin of a foreign public document affixed with an apostille is presumed to be sufficiently proven, unless the contrary is established.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This means that the apostille is presumed proof of: one, the authenticity of the signature on the document; two, the capacity in which the person signing the document has acted, in other words, the person's capacity to sign the document; and three, where appropriate, the identity of the seal or stamp that the document bears.

sections.label: Apostilles not mandatory
sections.summary: The Bill does not require apostilles to be used, unless as a replacement for legalisation imposed by certain Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill does not require apostilles to be used, unless as a replacement for the formality of legalisation which certain Government agencies may have imposed.

sections.label: Evidence Act apostille amendment
sections.summary: The amendment lets foreign public documents from Contracting Parties be proved by an apostille, without affecting Evidence Act provisions on proving public documents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: While the Evidence Act is not contrary to the obligations under the Apostille Convention, this amendment will allow for foreign public documents from Contracting Parties to also be proved by an apostille being affixed on such documents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The proposed amendment clarifies that the operation of Part 2 of the Bill is not affected by the sections of the Evidence Act which relate to the way in which public documents are proven.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These measures will streamline and modernise the process for authentication of public documents for recognition across different jurisdictions and no doubt, as I have said earlier, save time and expense for parties.

sections.label: Singapore joining Apostille Convention
sections.summary: If passed, Singapore will likely become party to the Apostille Convention next year, its 60th anniversary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If passed, Singapore will likely become party to the Apostille Convention next year which incidentally is the 60th anniversary of the Convention.

sections.label: One-step apostille process
sections.summary: With the Bill passed and the Convention ratified, the process is reduced to one step, and an apostille is recognised in about 118 countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: With the Apostille Bill passed and Singapore's ratification of the Apostille Convention, this is reduced to a one-step process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Not only that, as the hon Minister mentioned, the apostille once issued, is recognised in about 118 countries, which includes all the major countries in the world, the business centres in the world too.

sections.label: Average Convention country fee
sections.summary: The average fee among Convention countries as at 2016 was 15 Euros, about S$24.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: From my research, I noted that the average fee among Convention countries as at 2016 was 15 Euros, which translates to about S$24.

sections.label: Bill gives effect to Convention
sections.summary: The Bill gives effect to obligations under the Convention, streamlining recognition of foreign public documents and removing the need for two sets of authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill gives effect to our obligations under the Convention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This will streamline our processes for recognising foreign public documents and make it easier for our public documents to be recognised in other contracting states.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the apostille process in place, individuals will not have to go to two sets of government authorities to legalise foreign public documents.

sections.label: Apostille responsibility transfer to SAL
sections.summary: The member notes the transfer of apostille responsibility from MFA to SAL and seeks assurance that SAL will not increase current MFA fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I note the transfer of existing legalisation apostille responsibility from MFA to the Singapore Academy of Law or SAL, and that pursuant to this Bill, once passed, SAL will be the body issuing the relevant certificate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I have some concerns whether this will lead to an increase of the fees which are currently being charged by MFA for apostille related legalisation of documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While the intention for authentication is good and understandable, the change in the requirements resulted in additions to the process and paperwork, and additional charges to businesses and individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, I would like to seek the Minister's assurance that with the passing of this Bill, SAL will not increase the fees which are currently being charged by MFA in respect of any apostille certification charges.

sections.label: Decision to accede to Convention
sections.summary: Having satisfied itself it can accede and has the necessary infrastructure, it decided to proceed with the Convention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think it is true what he has said that his contributions from the backbench with his experience over several years, have contributed to our thinking on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We looked more closely at the Convention and eventually, having satisfied ourselves that it is a Convention that we can accede to and that we have the necessary infrastructure in place to play the role as envisaged in the Convention, we have decided to proceed with this.

sections.label: Digitalising the apostillisation process
sections.summary: SAL, the designated Competent Authority, is already working towards digitalising the entire apostillisation process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Both Mr Pillai and Mr Ng raised this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I am pleased to inform Mr Pillai and Mr Ng that SAL, which is the designated Competent Authority, is already working towards digitalising the entire apostillisation process.

sections.label: Apostille certificate fees
sections.summary: SAL intends to charge $10 for each apostille certificate at the inception.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For the apostille fees, SAL intends to charge $10 for each apostille certificate at the inception.

sections.label: Penal Code offences for false documents
sections.summary: Applying for an apostille on a false underlying document can be charged under Penal Code sections 471 read with 466.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is a serious offence and I agree with Mr Ng, but there is an existing framework now in the Penal Code to deal with this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, to Mr Ng's example of an academic certificate that is brought fraudulently or dishonestly, if one applies for an apostille on the basis of a false underlying document, then an offence under section 471 read with section 466 of the Penal Code, which is punishable with a term of imprisonment, that person can be charged under those offences.
